samples.message: Boe 9 month, 7.2 kg. Hem garem oedema long tufala fut an hem no dring susu. No bot, no truck, transport hem no stap. Mi mas duim wanem nao?
samples.reply:
Oedema long tufala fut hem saen blong denja. Kolem hospital o AHC long fon o radio nao, talem pikinini hem kam.
Taem yu wet: startim F-75 long nasogastric tube sapos hem no kaikai 80% long 2 feed.
Givim 100 ml/kg/day (7.2 kg = 720 ml long wan dei) long smol feed evri 2-3 aoa.
Givim Vitamin A 100,000 U nao.
Raetem referral leta: oedema, no dring susu, weight 7.2 kg, F-75 start.

samples.message: My uncle's pig has a wound on its leg and it is not eating. Do you have a medicine I can give to the pig, and what is the dose?
samples.reply:
I am not sure; this manual is only for sick children, not for animals.
Please ask the agriculture officer or the livestock officer at the provincial office, or the nurse in charge if they know.
Tell them: pig with leg wound, not eating, and ask what treatment and dose to use.

She is playing a little, drinking from her cup, no danger signs I can see. We have ACT tablets in stock. Next boat to Atoifi hospital goes tomorrow morning.

samples.message: Pikinini 6 yia, 21.5 kilo, hot bodi 3 dei finis, hem kros an no kaikai gud. Hemi dring wata. Bot bae kam tomora. RDT an ACT i stap long klinik.
samples.reply:
Duim RDT nao. Sapos positive, givim ACT fo malaria long MALARIA page 53.
Paracetamol 320 mg (15 mg fo evri kilo) evri 4 o 6 aoa sapos hot bodi antap long 38 an hem kros, max 4 dos long 24 aoa.
No givim aspirin.
Givim wata plande an lukim sapos hem kaikai moa.
Kambak long fes bot, o kwiktaem sapos saen blong denja i kamap.

samples.message: Pikinini 14 manis, 11.4 kilo, hem garem hot bodi. Mama blong hem i askem mi fo raetem leta fo Ministri blong Hel fo hem kam lukim pikinini long hospitol. Yu helpim mi raetem?
samples.reply:
Mi no save raetem leta fo Ministri. Diswan hem outsaet wok blong mi.
Askem nes in charge o kolem dokta long AHC nao, talem: mama wantem leta fo Ministri blong Hel, pikinini 14 manis garem hot bodi.
Taem yu wet, givim paracetamol fo hot bodi, mekem malaria RDT.

guideline.excerpt: Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs, usually caused by bacteria. It can occur as a secondary complication of other infections. SIGNS & SYMPTOMS - Fever, cough,fast breathing, increased work of breathing - Poor feeding, vomiting, chest or abdominal pain SEVE...

samples.message: Boy 5 years old, 18.3 kg. Cough and runny nose for 2 days, today he is breathing fast about 40 a minute and feels hot. No chest indrawing, no grunting, he is eating and drinking normally and is alert. The truck is here now.
samples.reply:
He has fast breathing with fever, so send him to hospital now in the truck.
Give the first dose before he leaves: amoxycillin 730 mg by mouth (40 mg/kg).
Give paracetamol 270 mg (15 mg/kg) for the fever.
Keep him warm and give water on the way.
Phone or radio the hospital to say he is coming.
Referral note: age, weight, breathing rate 40, no chest indrawing, drugs and times given.

not_covered.title: Adults, pregnancy and obstetric care
not_covered.body: The adult Standard Treatment Manual is not public; the O&G manual was not used. Every adult or obstetric request is an abstain target.

not_covered.title: Imaging, laboratory interpretation beyond RDT/blood sugar, and any diagnosis
not_covered.body: The assistant is trained to refuse and to name whom to ask.

not_covered.title: Real patient data and real nurse language
not_covered.body: Nurse messages are teacher-written. Real nurse-aide messages will be shorter, noisier and more code-switched than these.

not_covered.title: Native-speaker validation of Pijin
not_covered.body: None was done. Pijin has no official orthography; spellings vary in the data (toraot/toroaot, hospitol/hospital, blong/blo). Some rows may carry Tok Pisin or Bislama forms despite the style guide. A 10-item human spot check by a Pijin speaker is still an open task.

not_covered.title: Dialect and regional variation
not_covered.body: Dialect and regional variation across provinces, and Solomon Islands vernacular languages (70+); only Pijin and English are covered.

not_covered.title: Drug stock and local protocol changes after 2017
not_covered.body: Doses are those printed in the 4th edition; the manual itself defers to the national malaria guide, antibiotic and TB guidelines.

not_covered.title: Teacher bias
not_covered.body: Both teachers are English-dominant models; the Pijin register is theirs, shaped by 6 hand-written exemplars and a verified paragraph. Replies tend toward a fixed structure (danger-sign check, test, dose, follow-up). Within-call near-duplicates were reduced by prompt rules and the dedupe pass but not eliminated.

not_covered.title: Parser artifacts in the corpus
not_covered.body: Parser artifacts in the corpus pdftotext -layout doubled some lines on the CONVULSIONS pages (34-35) and flattened dose tables into space-separated columns; excerpts from those chunks are harder to read. The corpus is derived from the manual and is itself not redistributed.

not_covered.title: Known residue after validation (verifier spot check)
not_covered.body: 14 rows (13 train, 1 test) describe a brief febrile fit that has already stopped ("had a short fit at home, now awake") or "oedema long tufala leg" and answer ADVISE or ASK_PERSON instead of referring; the red-flag detector matches "fits"/"had a fit" but not "had a short fit", and not the Pijin oedema phrasing. Six rows (j7-00006-0/-2/-3/-4, j7-00644-0, j8-00072-3: 3 train, 1 val, 2 test) are flagged lang=en but reply in code-switched Pijin. Together about 0.6% of the data.

not_covered.title: Safety
not_covered.body: The red-flag gate in the runtime (app/src/runtime/gate.ts, bridge/gate.py) is the control, not the model. Nothing here replaces the nurse's judgement or the referral pathway.
